key_insight: A projectability-guided AO Hamiltonian construction lets deep-learning models learn compact, accurate plane-wave DFT targets while retaining nonlocal hybrid-functional effects.
engineering_relevance: This makes plane-wave DFT data more usable for scalable electronic-structure prediction, reducing basis size without sacrificing band-structure accuracy.
method: Select high-projectability PW eigenstates and use extra higher-energy states to complete the AO subspace.
Build nonorthogonal AO Hamiltonians directly from PW eigenvalues/eigenstates, avoiding an empirical energy shift.
Train equivariant neural networks on the resulting PBE/HSE Hamiltonians for prediction.
evidence_signal: Benchmarks on MoS2 and sodium phases show the reconstructed AO Hamiltonians reproduce PW band structures accurately with smaller AO bases than real-space reconstruction.
watch_item: The approach depends on carefully choosing the retained PW states and completion states, so subspace selection may affect accuracy and transferability.
paper_title: Accurately Generalizing Deep-Learning Hamiltonian Methods to Plane-Wave Density Functional Theory
